name: HCA Gut Cell Atlas v1 Stromal Lineage
description: Healthy and adjacent-to-disease control data from 27 gut single-cell RNAseq datasets were collected and integrated to form v1 of the Human Gut Cell Atlas stromal lineage

labels.name: doublets
labels.rationale: A Cell Annotation Platform (CAP) term used to identify a row in a “cell by gene” table that appears to contain combined data from a pair of cells rather than data from one cell and should therefore be discarded.

labels.name: Epithelial
labels.rationale: Cells of other lineages are sometimes sorted by the border of broad clusters. These appear to be epithelial cells

labels.name: Smooth Muscle Cells (SMC)
labels.rationale: Expresses DES, TAGLN, MYH11, ACTG2 consistent with visceral smooth muscle layers of gut wall (muscularis propria/longitudinal and circular layers).

labels.name: Fibroblasts Lamina propria (S1)
labels.rationale: This label represents superficial lamina propria fibroblasts that are ADAMDEC1+, ABCA8+, FABP4+ and form the dominant fibroblast population across datasets and samples. FOS+ Fibroblast Lamina propria or Ribo(high) Fibroblast Lamina propria, and note an upper-lamina WNT4+ subset (Stroma_0_2) described in the literature, as well as plasma (IGHA+) and myeloid (C1S/C1R+) doublet-contaminated clusters. Taken together, the transcriptional program, high dataset and sample diversity, and literature on WNT4+ villus-oriented fibroblasts support a high-confidence lamina propria fibroblast identity, with FOS and ribosomal signatures reflecting activation state rather than separate cell types.

labels.name: vascular endothelial Venular
labels.rationale: Annotated by ACKR1 predominantly, these separate clearly from other vascular endothelial clusters

labels.name: Fibroblasts Crypt Bottom (S2A)
labels.rationale: S2A fibroblasts sit near the crypt base and are enriched for VSTM2A together with PDGFRA, BMP4, WNT5A, POSTN and other S2 markers. Several clusters annotated as Fibroblasts Crypt Bottom (S2A) show very low dataset diversity but reproducible expression of POSTN, F3 and BMPs, and differences between individual S2A annotation clusters are subtle (see annotation_cluster) and may largely reflect activation and quality flags (for example high mitochondrial content) rather than true subtypes. We therefore annotate a single S2A cell type corresponding to crypt-bottom fibroblasts with high-confidence positional identity and variable activation signatures.

labels.name: Fibroblasts Crypt Top (S2B)
labels.rationale: S2B fibroblasts are positioned toward the crypt top or villus tip and are characterized by NRG1 and NPY, we also highlight VEGFD and TRPA1 as convincing markers of villus-tip subepithelial fibroblasts. Clusters annotated as Fibroblasts Crypt Top (S2B) (for example Stroma_1_1 and 12_1–12_4) show these markers along with the broader S2 program and are present in multiple datasets, albeit with varying mitochondrial content and dataset diversity. We therefore treat S2B as a robust positional subtype of S2, capturing villus-tip fibroblasts with strong NRG1/VEGFD/TRPA1 signatures.

labels.name: vascular endothelial Arteriolar
labels.rationale: Arteriolar endothelial cells express SEMA3G, PLVAP, TM4SF1, MGP

labels.name: vascular endothelial Pre venule capillary (PVC)
labels.rationale: Identified by LITAF and ICAM1 expression, consistent with pre venous capillary beds positioned before venules in intestinal microcirculation.

labels.name: Fibroblasts Subserosal
labels.rationale: Fibroblasts annotated as Subserosal are enriched for DPT, C7 and POSTN and tend to form deeper fibroblast clusters with lower dataset diversity (for example Stroma_8_0 and 8_1). We note that some clusters labeled as Subserosal in the original annotations appear in many biopsy-derived datasets, so we question whether they are truly subserosal versus generally deeper S3 fibroblasts. Do we need a deeper S3 fibroblast annotation? We therefore sometimes use the Intestinal Subserosal Fibroblasts and sometimes S3 term for DPT+/C7+/POSTN+ deeper fibroblasts while acknowledging that the exact boundary between subserosal and submucosal S3 fibroblasts is still being refined.

labels.name: Fibroblasts Subepithelial (S2)
labels.rationale: S2 fibroblasts form a subepithelial band under the epithelium and are characterized by PDGFRA, BMP4, F3, NPY, CD34, TRPA1, SOX6, WNT5A and POSTN expression. Multiple clusters are noted as FOS+ Fibroblast Subepithelial with clear POSTN, F3 and BMP signatures and we note that TRPA1 and VEGFD are good markers higher in the villus axis, while VSTM2A and NRG1 mark bottom and top crypt positions respectively. These clusters are present across many datasets with varying activation and mitochondrial signatures, suggesting a continuum of S2 fibroblast states rather than distinct cell types.

labels.name: vascular endothelial Post arteriole capillary (PAC)
labels.rationale: RGCC and FCN3, distinguishing it from pre venule capillaries and venules in gut vasculature.

labels.name: Glia Myenteric Plexus / Type I
labels.rationale: Myenteric plexus type I glia are identified by TF, BCAN and CACLB expression on top of a pan-glial program, and occupy clusters that align with deeper muscularis propria / submucosal regions in the integrated object. These clusters are present across datasets with full-thickness or muscularis-enriched sampling, consistent with myenteric plexus localization. The glial subtypes performed poorly in reference mapping benchmarks, so a lesser resolution is likely best for the data currently. Annotation experts also point to less confidence in glial subtypes

labels.name: Glia Submucosal Plexus / Type I
labels.rationale: This label is used for type I glia associated with the submucosal plexus, distinguished by expression of ENTPD2, SFRP5 and a core glial program and by their co-clustering with other submucosal plexus markers in integrated data. They are present across several datasets but enriched in samples with preserved submucosa, consistent with a submucosal plexus localization. The glial subtypes performed poorly in reference mapping benchmarks, so a lesser resolution is likely best for the data currently. Annotation experts also point to less confidence in glial subtypes

labels.name: Pericytes Secretory
labels.rationale: MUSTN1 and PLN were used to annotate pericytes with secretory program, two putative paracrine factors

labels.name: Fibroblasts Muscularis Propria
labels.rationale: These fibroblasts are defined by DPT, C7, KCNN3, CA8 and PLCB4 expression and were initially annotated as Muscularis Propria fibroblasts in the hierarchy, but our experts repeatedly note that some clusters with this label are present in many biopsy-derived datasets, which is difficult to reconcile with a strictly muscularis-only population. Marker profiles suggest a deeper S3-like or muscle-adjacent fibroblast population, but current spatial evidence is insufficient to cleanly separate muscularis propria fibroblasts from subserosal or submucosal fibroblasts in the integrated data. We therefore keep this label as a provisional deeper muscle-layer fibroblast class with moderate confidence and flag the spatial assignment as uncertain. Do we need a "deep S3" sub-label?
labels.ontologyAssessment: Do we need a "deep S3 fibroblast" sublabel?

labels.name: Glia Mucosal/Type III
labels.rationale: Mucosal type III glia are defined by RELN, MBP and PLLP expression together with canonical glial markers, and are the predominant glial population in mucosa/submucosa-enriched samples. Several clusters annotated as Glia Mucosal/Type III recur across many datasets, suggesting a conserved mucosal glial state. We therefore treat this as a robust mucosal glial subtype with moderate-confidence mapping to the CL type 3 mucosal glia term. The glial subtypes performed poorly in reference mapping benchmarks, so a lesser resolution is likely best for the data currently. Annotation experts also point to less confidence in glial subtypes

labels.name: SMC Inner Muscle Cells
labels.rationale: SMC with FOXF2 and MORN5, likely inner circular smooth muscle layer of gut wall. Tissue section should be checked for these to ensure not myofibroblast

labels.name: Glia Extra-Ganglionic
labels.rationale: This label is used for enteric glia captured outside of well-formed myenteric and submucosal ganglia, especially in biopsy-derived datasets. Clusters annotated as Glia Extra-Ganglionic show a broad glial program (NRXN1, S100B, SOX10, PLP1) without clear plexus-restricted signatures and are the dominant glial population in mucosal samples.
labels.ontologyAssessment: need a term for glia on enteric neurons outside the ganglia (mucosa enervating neuron glia)

labels.name: junk
labels.rationale: A Cell Annotation Platform (CAP) term used to identify a row in a “cell by gene” table that appears to contain non-cellular data rather than data from one cell and should therefore be discarded.

labels.name: Fibroblastic reticular cells
labels.rationale: Fibroblastic reticular cells are defined by expression of CCL19, CCL21, TNFSF13B and CXCL13 and cluster within lymphoid-enriched regions, consistent with FRCs organizing lymphoid tissue. Multiple clusters labeled as Fibroblastic reticular cells show similar marker profiles across datasets and samples, while a related cluster (Stroma_19_0) expresses RANKL and CXCL14 and may correspond to mesenchymal lymphoid tissue organizer cells. We note that FRC and mLTo-like states have some overlap. we annotate them with the intestinal fibroblastic reticular cell term and note the close relationship to mLTo.

labels.name: Pericytes Angiogenic
labels.rationale: HIGD1B expression marks pericytes engaged in vascular sprouting and angiogenesis

labels.name: SMC Outer Muscle Cells
labels.rationale: Outer longitudinal layer smooth muscle; distinguished from IMC by low FOXF2. Tissue section should be checked for these to ensure not myofibroblast

labels.name: vascular endothelial
labels.rationale: This grouping term is used for generic vascular endothelial cells expressing PECAM1, CDH5 and PLVAP that do not clearly fall into arteriolar, capillary, venular or lymphatic categories. Experts here noted that some clusters labeled vascular endothelial contain AQP1 and fibroblast genes and may represent mixed, transitional, or unclearly clustered states, and that there are doublet clusters involving endothelial cells and S2 fibroblasts. It's just one subcluster here that could be refined further with more evidence

labels.name: Pericytes Contractile
labels.rationale: Defined by RERGL and NTRK2, suggesting a pericyte subset with enhanced contractile apparatus.

labels.name: Glia Intra-Ganglionic
labels.rationale: This label corresponds to glia located within enteric ganglia, matching the type I enteric glial cell definition and showing enrichment for APOE, FRZB, RLBP1, CRYM and other neuro-supportive genes. Clusters annotated as Glia Intra-Ganglionic are present across multiple datasets and sit transcriptionally between myenteric and submucosal plexus glia, consistent with the canonical intra-ganglionic location.

labels.name: vascular endothelial Lymphatic
labels.rationale: Lymphatic endothelial cells are here defined by LYVE1, PROX1, MMRN1 and MRC1 and form multiple clusters (Stroma_13_1–13_5) that are present across many datasets, including immune-interacting states.

labels.name: vascular endothelial Capillary
labels.rationale: CD36, CLDN5, RAMP2, FLT1 and IGFBP7, consistent with gut micro capillary networks described in human intestinal single cell atlases.

labels.name: vascular endothelial Lacteals
labels.rationale: Lacteals here were annotated due to a strong fatty acid and glycerol uptake program. We should check if stroma_13_0 are present mostly in duodenum, consistent with villus lacteals being more prominent in small intestine. RELN here points to crypt

labels.name: Pericytes Immature
labels.rationale: We identified these with NDUFA4L2, PDGFRB and CSPG4 expression. Not sure about the latter two.

labels.name: Fibroblasts mLTo Cells (mesenchymal lymphoid tissue organizer cells)
labels.rationale: Clusters annotated as Fibroblasts mLTo Cells show expression of RANKL (TNFSF11), CXCL14 and other lymphoid-organizing genes in addition to a fibroblast matrix program, and Stroma_19_0 especially "could be mLTo because RANKL, CXCL14, TNFSF11". These cells likely represent a specialized organizer subset related to fibroblastic reticular cells but with stronger RANKL-driven lymphoid organizing functions. The population is relatively small and has moderate dataset diversity, consistent with tissue-restricted lymphoid niches, so we annotate it as a candidate mesenchymal lymphoid tissue organizer fibroblast class.

labels.name: Plasma Cells
labels.rationale: Cells of other lineages are sometimes sorted by the border of broad clusters. These appear to be plasma cells

labels.name: Fibroblasts Myofibroblasts
labels.rationale: Myofibroblasts and SMCs could be mixed up in some places. I had used HHIF to annotated SMCs but in absense of GREM1/GREM2 it's possible these SMCs are really myofibroblasts.

labels.name: Glia Muscularis propria/Type IV
labels.rationale: This label captures glia associated with the muscularis propria that show markers such as SLC5A7, APOD and KCNS3 in addition to a core glial program. These clusters are enriched in full-thickness specimens with abundant muscle, and rare or absent in superficial biopsies, consistent with a muscularis propria localization.  The glial subtypes performed poorly in reference mapping benchmarks, so a lesser resolution is likely best for the data currently. Annotation experts also point to less confidence in glial subtypes

labels.name: Fibroblasts Submucosal (aka Crypt Support/Trophocytes/S3)
labels.rationale: Submucosal S3 fibroblasts occupy deeper layers and crypt base regions and are enriched for GREM1, C7, OLFM4, PTGS2, THY1, SEMA3A and GLI1, consistent with crypt-support or trophocyte roles. Cluster-level annotations describe RSPO3, GREM1, DCN and C3 as strong markers of submucosal fibroblasts (for example Stroma_2_0) and we note that S3 populations have lower dataset diversity and appear deeper than lamina propria fibroblasts, especially in resection-derived data. Multiple clusters labeled as Fibroblasts Submucosal (aka Crypt Support/Trophocytes/S3) recur with similar signatures, supporting a distinct S3 fibroblast class even though a dedicated CL term is still needed.
